NEW FINDINGS FROM FRESH SOURCE VERIFICATION (this pass, beyond what the fifth gate checked)

CRITICAL — a new false, self-contradicting claim introduced BY this fix commit while correcting a different citation.
Location: Problem Statement, line 69: "the table exists, and the FK is in place (`fk-004-chunks-collection-registry.xml`, ...; `fk-002` created the registry table)."
Problem: Verified against source: fk-002-collection-registry.xml contains zero CREATE TABLE statements (grepped `createTable`/`CREATE TABLE` — no hits). It only ADDs foreign keys FROM the chunk tables TO the already-existing catalog_collections table. The table itself is created by catalog-001-baseline.xml's changeset `catalog-001-5` (grep-confirmed) — which is exactly what RDR-204's OWN Relationship table says fifty lines later, at line 119: "RDR-101 ... Created `catalog_collections` ... (changeset catalog-001-5)." So the document now contradicts itself about who created the table, and the newer claim (added by 606f530db, the commit meant to fix the fk-002/fk-004 citation) is the false one.
Impact: This is the exact defect class (miscited changeset provenance) this RDR has now hit five times — three missed-table hand-lists/FK-derivation attempts on COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES, the fk-002/fk-004 swap the fifth gate caught, and now this, introduced by the commit that fixed the fourth. A reader or future implementer citing "fk-002 created the registry table" would be citing something false and internally contradicted by the RDR's own Relationship table.
Recommendation: Drop the fk-002 clause entirely, or replace with "`fk-002` created the earlier per-dimension chunk FKs it superseded" (matching fk-002's actual content) — never "created the registry table." The table's creation is already correctly attributed at line 119; do not re-attribute it here.
Evidence: `grep -n "CREATE TABLE\|createTable" service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/fk-002-collection-registry.xml` → no hits. `grep -rln 'createTable.*tableName="catalog_collections"' service/src/main/resources/db/changelog/*.xml` → catalog-001-baseline.xml only, changeSet id="catalog-001-5".
Ship-blocker: yes — a fabricated, self-contradicting provenance claim in an RDR whose whole subject is "the table nobody trusted" should not survive to accept.

SIGNIFICANT — redundant-clause fix landed at one site, left stale at a second.
Location: Implementation Plan, Phase 1 item 1, line ~608: "the ghost sweep through `collectionIsEmpty` plus the `physical_collection` check, then the walk..."
Problem: This bullet was NOT touched by commit 606f530db (confirmed absent from the diff) and still frames the sweep as two separate checks. It directly contradicts Technical Design step 3, two sections above, freshly corrected by this same commit to say the physical_collection/catalog_documents clause is redundant and dropped ("`catalog_documents.physical_collection` is one of the fourteen entries that predicate checks, so it needs no separate clause"). The fifth gate's observation ("trim the redundant clause for clarity") was fixed at the Technical Design site only; the Implementation Plan's mirror of the same mechanism was missed.
Recommendation: Change Phase 1 item 1 to "the ghost sweep through `collectionIsEmpty` (which already covers `physical_collection` via `catalog_documents`), then the walk..." or simply drop "plus the `physical_collection` check" — matching the corrected Technical Design wording.
Ship-blocker: no.

SIGNIFICANT — "refuses" reused for `collectionIsEmpty` itself, undoing the precision Finding A just established, in the same paragraph.
Location: Technical Design step 3, line 422: "A row `collectionIsEmpty` refuses on is kept and becomes `dormant` (below)." Repeated at Phase 1 item 5, line 623: "ghost sweep deletes the unreferenced and keeps the referenced" — wait, actually at line 623 the phrase is "the sweep keeps a row that `collectionIsEmpty` refuses on for EACH table in `COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES`" (test enumeration).
Problem: `collectionIsEmpty` is a boolean predicate (`private boolean collectionIsEmpty(DSLContext ctx, String name) { return blockingTable(ctx, name).isEmpty(); }`, line 6818-6819) — it does not refuse anything; it reports true or false. Two sentences earlier, in the same paragraph, this same commit fixed the text to say exactly that distinction: "`renameCollectionTxn` refuses a merge on it, and `deleteCollectionTxn` cascades over the same list [without refusing]." Reusing "refuses" as a verb attached to `collectionIsEmpty` at line 422 and again at line 623 reintroduces the category error Finding A spent three gate rounds correcting, just with the boot-job sweep standing in for deleteCollectionTxn instead of deleteCollectionTxn itself.
Recommendation: Line 422 → "A row `collectionIsEmpty` reports non-empty for is kept and becomes `dormant`." Line 623 → "the sweep keeps a row `collectionIsEmpty` reports non-empty for, for EACH table in `COLLECTION_SCOPED_TABLES`."
Ship-blocker: no. Not introduced by this commit (pre-existing, uncaught by five prior passes), but squarely inside the vocabulary this commit was supposed to make consistent.
